title: With All Eyes On These Guys, This Play Is A Nice Surprise

contact_edits.before: The hostage-takers are kept offstage, like a collective Godot though one whose appearance is dreaded rather than desired. We don't even hear much about them. Here the play cheats; it may be the captors' strategy to keep the captives physically in the light (it's never switched off) and mentally in the dark (they don't even know what day it is) but they must have said something. They must be making demands of some kind, or why take hostages at all? But the characters say nothing about it, apparently keeping quiet for our benefit. We don't even know if they've been physically ill-treated; there are bruises on Ferry's legs but they're never explained or even referred to. The tensions and resolutions between the cellmates are finely dramatized, their ongoing fight with their jailers not so much: a limitation that's frustrating but that may also, paradoxically, be a strength. There is a fourth voice written into the play, that of Ella Fitzgerald, whose recording of the almost title song (the Gershwins called it Someone to Watch Over Me) is both Edward's choice of imaginary Desert Island Disc and a key to the theme of both play and production: interdependence. - Someone Who'll Watch Over Me is at the Berkeley Street Theatre Upstairs in Toronto until Dec. 13. Call 416-368-3110 for tickets and information.
